mathematical_or_operational_scope: Recursive ZIP byte-provenance inventory for the 16:28 addition; no mathematical theorem is checked.
positive_controls: Lines 12–23 reject excessive recursion, member counts, advertised expansion, absolute/traversal/backslash paths, archive symlinks, and duplicate file names; cumulative decompressed bytes are capped.
Lines 28–32 preserve every file occurrence and deduplicate canonical byte hashes. Lines 60–62 explicitly separate byte novelty from mathematical novelty.

findings.issue: All structural limits and the final failure gate use assert; optimized Python removes them. This is an unsuitable adversarial acceptance boundary unless optimization is forbidden or explicit exceptions replace assertions.

Manifest presence/completeness is not enforced. An empty source_archives directory or archives without a recognized manifest produce zero verification failures. A manifest checks only its named entries; it cannot establish that every member is committed.
A manifest reference can resolve relative to its manifest or archive root, and any hash-matching candidate passes. This compatibility rule is not a unique canonical path interpretation.
Outputs are written before the terminal manifest-failure assertion; failure can leave apparently complete inventory artifacts behind.

cost_and_scaling: O(B) hashing plus manifest rereads for B total recursively decompressed bytes. Holds all uncompressed members of each active archive and the input ZIP in memory. Top-level ZIP bytes are read before a compressed-input size cap; cumulative bounds are assertion-based.
test_scope_and_limits: No tests executed in this review. The source defines runtime safety/manifest assertions but no adversarial unit tests, known-prior schema validation, or required archive-count check.
certificate_acceptance: Accepts identity against the declared prior and manifests only. It neither authenticates that prior nor proves content completeness, authorship, mathematical novelty, or source correctness.
